question: Why are rest stations sometimes included in an OSCE circuit?

question: What kind of clinical scenarios should educators focus on for OSCE stations?

question: What is the main function of an objective checklist in an OSCE?

question: How should an examiner generally behave during an active OSCE station?

question: Why are faculty calibration sessions important before holding an OSCE?

options.C: To change the examination questions based on student gossip

question: What is the main purpose of holding a mock OSCE before the real exam?

question: How does reviewing sample checklists with peers help a midwifery student prepare?

question: Which of the following is a common challenge when running OSCEs in large schools?

question: Why are written multiple-choice exams alone not enough to evaluate midwifery students on the labor ward?

question: What does a clear rubric give a midwifery student before starting a clinical posting?

question: If two different teachers give widely different scores for the exact same student performance, what quality is this rubric lacking?

question: How should a rubric measure a concept like 'good bedside manner'?

options.B: By letting patients vote anonymously in a suggestion box after discharge
options.C: By measuring how many polite greetings the student gives per hour
options.D: By listing concrete visible actions such as explaining procedures and obtaining consent

explanation: Effective rubrics replace vague traits with specific, observable behaviors that can be clearly seen and ticked off. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T11#BMP312_U3_T11_h3)

question: At which level is a midwifery student able to perform routine tasks safely, even if they still lack overall speed and efficiency?

options.A: Proficient
options.B: Competent
options.C: Novice
options.D: Advanced Beginner

explanation: An advanced beginner has moved past the initial learning stage and can work safely under routine conditions, though not yet at full expert speed. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T11#BMP312_U3_T11_h3)

question: What is the 'halo effect' in clinical evaluation?

options.A: Allowing a positive trait like a pleasant personality to mask clinical errors
options.B: Forgetting to grade a student's practical workbook before the deadline
options.C: Giving every single student the highest possible score to avoid conflict
options.D: Failing a student immediately upon making the very first minor mistake

explanation: The halo effect causes evaluators to judge an entire performance based on one prominent positive impression. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T11#BMP312_U3_T11_h4)

question: A preceptor gives a student low marks for an unrelated physical examination skill simply because the student arrived five minutes late. Which bias is this?

options.A: The halo effect
options.B: Observer fatigue
options.C: Evaluator leniency
options.D: The horn effect

explanation: The horn effect occurs when a negative impression in one area unfairly influences the evaluation of other completely separate skills. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T11#BMP312_U3_T11_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a good characteristic of clinical feedback?

options.A: Delayed until the very end of the final semester examinations
options.B: Timely discussion shortly after the observed clinical procedure
options.C: Specific references to documented items on the rubric sheet
options.D: Focused on practical strategies for clinical improvement

explanation: Feedback must be given promptly while the clinical event is still fresh in the minds of both student and preceptor. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T11#BMP312_U3_T11_h5)

question: Why should a preceptor point to specific sections of the rubric during feedback instead of just giving a final score?

options.A: To connect the grade directly to observable behaviors and guide future improvement
options.B: To waste time so that less clinical paperwork needs to be completed
options.C: To ensure the paper work is filled completely to satisfy the school board
options.D: To prove to the student that the preceptor is always right

explanation: Using rubric details helps the student understand exactly where they succeeded and where they need to practice more. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T11#BMP312_U3_T11_h5)

question: What is the main focus of a behavioral learning objective?

options.A: What the student should be able to do
options.B: What topics the lecturer plans to read
options.C: Which textbook the students must buy
options.D: How many hours the class will last

explanation: Behavioral objectives target what the student can actually do rather than the teacher's classroom activities. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T2#BMP312_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why are clear learning objectives useful in midwifery clinical training?

options.A: They reduce the number of hours spent in the labor ward
options.B: They guarantee that students will never fail an exam
options.C: They provide a fair basis for practical assessments
options.D: They eliminate the need for clinical demonstration

explanation: Clear objectives set transparent standards so both the student and the examiner know what competency is being tested. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T2#BMP312_U3_T2_h1)

question: What does the letter 'B' stand for in the ABC formula of learning objectives?

options.A: Bulletin
options.B: Behavior
options.C: Booklet
options.D: Baseline

explanation: The B stands for behavior, representing the specific action the student will perform. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T2#BMP312_U3_T2_h2)

question: In this objective, which part is the condition: 'Given a partograph, the student midwife will plot cervical dilation accurately.'?

options.A: accurately
options.B: will plot cervical dilation
options.C: the student midwife
options.D: Given a partograph

explanation: The condition describes the tools or context provided to the learner when performing the task. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T2#BMP312_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the three main domains of Bloom's taxonomy?

options.A: Psychomotor domain
options.B: Financial domain
options.C: Affective domain
options.D: Cognitive domain

explanation: The three recognized domains are cognitive, psychomotor, and affective. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T2#BMP312_U3_T2_h3)

question: Why must midwifery educators teach across all three domains of Bloom's taxonomy?

options.A: Physical skills are completely useless without passing written theory papers
options.B: Midwifery requires mental knowledge, physical skills, and compassionate attitudes
options.C: University regulations strictly punish lecturers who focus on only one domain
options.D: The affective domain is the only area tested during national board exams

explanation: A complete midwife needs intellect, practical skills, and professional empathy to care for mothers safely. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T2#BMP312_U3_T2_h3)

question: What is the foundational level of learning in the cognitive domain?

options.A: Evaluating
options.B: Creating
options.C: Remembering
options.D: Applying

explanation: Remembering is the basic level where students recall previously learned information from memory. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T2#BMP312_U3_T2_h4)

question: Which cognitive level is used when a student calculates drug dosages for a newborn?

options.A: Evaluating
options.B: Applying
options.C: Remembering
options.D: Creating

explanation: Using learned rules and formulas in a new clinical situation represents the application level. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T2#BMP312_U3_T2_h4)

question: What do psychomotor objectives primarily focus on in midwifery training?

options.A: Memorization of anatomical terminology
options.B: Physical execution of clinical procedures
options.C: Development of emotional empathy for clients
options.D: Understanding historical trends in healthcare

explanation: Psychomotor objectives deal directly with hands-on manual tasks and bodily coordination. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T2#BMP312_U3_T2_h5)

question: What happens when a student midwife reaches the final stage of mastering a practical skill?

options.A: The student requires constant correction from supervisors
options.B: The procedure takes much longer to complete safely
options.C: The skill is performed smoothly and automatically
options.D: The student relies entirely on step-by-step reading

explanation: At this stage, muscle memory is well established, allowing the student to execute the procedure effortlessly. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T2#BMP312_U3_T2_h5)

question: What type of student growth does the affective domain measure?

options.A: Feelings, attitudes, and professional values
options.B: Memorization of obstetric terminology
options.C: Calculation of intravenous drug dosages
options.D: Manual dexterity in performing sutures

explanation: The affective domain focuses on emotions, values, ethics, and professional disposition. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T2#BMP312_U3_T2_h6)

question: Why is it often difficult to write and assess objectives in the affective domain?

options.A: Midwifery students already possess perfect bedside manners
options.B: Regulatory bodies forbid grading students on how they feel
options.C: There are no written textbooks available for professional ethics
options.D: Internal feelings and attitudes are not directly visible

explanation: Because attitudes are internal, educators rely on observable actions, like polite speech, to assess affective learning. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T2#BMP312_U3_T2_h6)

question: Which of these verbs is too vague for writing a measurable behavioral objective?

options.A: Demonstrate
options.B: Understand
options.C: List
options.D: Calculate

explanation: 'Understand' describes an internal mental state that cannot be directly observed, making it unmeasurable. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T2#BMP312_U3_T2_h7)

question: Which action verb fits a learning objective at the evaluating level of Bloom's taxonomy?

options.A: List
options.B: State
options.C: Define
options.D: Critique

explanation: Critique requires making judgments based on criteria, which fits the evaluating tier. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T2#BMP312_U3_T2_h7)

question: What is a common error when writing behavioral objectives?

options.A: Including conditions and degrees of performance
options.B: Describing what the teacher will do instead of the student
options.C: Focusing exclusively on measurable clinical outcomes
options.D: Using active action verbs at the beginning of the sentence

explanation: Objectives must center on student performance and learning outcomes, not teacher activities. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T2#BMP312_U3_T2_h8)

question: Why is it a mistake to put multiple learning actions into a single objective statement?

options.A: It automatically lowers the cognitive level of the lesson
options.B: It makes grading and assessing student competence confusing
options.C: It prevents students from attending clinical postings
options.D: It forces the lecturer to use unmeasurable verbs

explanation: Single-action objectives ensure that if a student struggles, the examiner knows precisely which skill or knowledge needs work. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T2#BMP312_U3_T2_h8)

question: What primary document acts as the master blueprint for guiding what student midwives learn during their training?

options.A: A clinical duty roster
options.B: A midwifery curriculum
options.C: A student attendance log
options.D: A hospital budget report

explanation: A curriculum outlines the overall plan, subjects, and learning experiences required for a programme of study. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T3#BMP312_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why must midwifery training programs in Nigeria match national health goals, such as lowering maternal mortality?

options.A: To ensure student midwives address the specific health needs of local communities
options.B: To eliminate the need for clinical hospital postings
options.C: To focus exclusively on international nursing standards
options.D: To make the training programme shorter and less expensive

explanation: Aligning education with local health realities ensures graduates possess the exact skills required to save lives in their practice environments. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T3#BMP312_U3_T3_h1)

question: What is the main focus of competency-based midwifery education?

options.A: Passing written examinations without practical tests
options.B: Demonstrating specific, measurable clinical skills
options.C: Memorising the history of global nursing leaders
options.D: Completing a fixed number of hours sitting in lectures

explanation: Competency-based education prioritises the actual performance and mastery of practical tasks over time spent in a classroom. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T3#BMP312_U3_T3_h2)

question: A student midwife is observed performing newborn resuscitation on a mannequin to prove she can handle an emergency before going to the labour ward. What type of assessment is this?

options.A: Passive observation
options.B: Administrative review
options.C: Summative assessment
options.D: Curriculum audit

explanation: Evaluating a student to verify mastery of a required skill before granting clinical clearance functions as a summative check. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T3#BMP312_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which of these is an example of an action word that can be easily measured in a clinical learning objective?

options.A: Understand
options.B: Demonstrate
options.C: Know
options.D: Appreciate

explanation: Demonstrate is an observable action that an examiner can watch and grade, unlike abstract words like understand or appreciate. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T3#BMP312_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why do midwifery educators avoid using the word 'understand' when writing learning objectives?

options.A: It prevents students from asking questions in class
options.B: It is grammatically incorrect in professional writing
options.C: It is only used for advanced postgraduate research courses
options.D: It is too vague and difficult to measure objectively

explanation: Because internal understanding cannot be directly seen, objectives require external, observable actions to prove mastery. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T3#BMP312_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of a lesson plan in midwifery education?

options.A: To replace the official school curriculum entirely
options.B: To record the disciplinary history of student midwives
options.C: To serve as a structured roadmap for a single teaching session
options.D: To track the monthly salary of the teaching staff

explanation: A lesson plan guides the instructor step-by-step through a specific class period to ensure all learning goals are met. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T3#BMP312_U3_T3_h4)

question: What is the main function of the introduction phase in a well-structured lesson plan?

options.A: To capture student attention and connect new material to prior knowledge
options.B: To clean up the clinical demonstration laboratory
options.C: To administer the final grade for the entire semester
options.D: To dismiss the students early from class

explanation: An effective introduction hooks the learners and prepares their minds by bridging what they already know with what they are about to learn. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T3#BMP312_U3_T3_h4)

question: Which teaching method works best for training student midwives to repair an episiotomy before working on real patients?

options.A: A large hall lecture on health history
options.B: A silent written reading assignment
options.C: An independent library research essay
options.D: Clinical simulation and demonstration

explanation: Hands-on demonstration and simulation allow students to practice psychomotor skills safely before performing them on mothers. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T3#BMP312_U3_T3_h5)

question: A lecturer wants students to practice critical thinking by discussing a real patient scenario involving severe pre-eclampsia. Which teaching strategy should they choose?

options.A: A physical fitness drill
options.B: Rote memorisation of medical terms
options.C: Silent individual textbook reading
options.D: Case study analysis

explanation: Case studies present realistic clinical problems that challenge students to apply diagnostic reasoning and decision-making skills. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T3#BMP312_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of an Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE) in midwifery training?

options.A: To assess administrative leadership skills in hospital management
options.B: To grade the cleanliness of the student uniform
options.C: To evaluate practical clinical competence through timed stations
options.D: To test long-term memory using long essay questions

explanation: An OSCE uses structured stations where students perform specific clinical tasks while examiners score them against objective checklists. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T3#BMP312_U3_T3_h6)

question: What should a midwifery school do when multiple students consistently fail a specific clinical skill assessment?

options.A: Blame the external regulatory body for the examination questions
options.B: Review and revise the curriculum, lesson plans, and teaching methods
options.C: Remove all practical assessments from the programme permanently
options.D: Assume the students are simply lazy and increase the passing mark

explanation: Widespread failure often signals a gap in how the material is taught or structured, requiring educators to evaluate and improve their own instruction. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T3#BMP312_U3_T3_h6)

question: What is the main feature of the classic lecture teaching method?

options.A: It focuses solely on practical bedside patient care
options.B: It requires students to work in small clinical groups
options.C: It relies entirely on independent student computer research
options.D: It is a teacher-centred oral presentation of information

explanation: A lecture is basically an oral presentation delivered by the instructor to a group of learners. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why is the lecture method often used for large classes in nursing and midwifery schools?

options.A: It ensures students spend most of their time in the hospital wards
options.B: It guarantees that every student passes their final board examinations
options.C: It allows efficient delivery of foundational theory to many students at once
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any clinical demonstrations

explanation: Lecturing lets a single educator share basic theory with a large group of students at the same time, saving time and resources. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h1)

question: How does communication usually flow during the main part of a traditional lecture?

options.A: Constant collaborative debate among all attending learners
options.B: Unidirectional flow from the lecturer to the students
options.C: Peer-to-peer teaching led exclusively by senior students
options.D: Strictly digital communication through mobile messaging apps

explanation: Traditional lecturing involves the instructor talking and the students listening, which is a one-way path of sharing information. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h2)

question: What skill does a lecturer rely on most to keep students focused during a long talk?

options.A: Physical stamina for running around the lecture hall
options.B: Strong verbal articulation and deep subject command
options.C: Advanced computer programming and software design
options.D: Expertise in staging theatrical drama productions

explanation: When there are no interactive activities, a clear voice, good pacing, and a strong knowledge of the topic help keep the audience interested. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h2)

question: What is a major organizational advantage of using lectures for large classes?

options.A: It replaces all textbook reading with audio recordings
options.B: It accommodates many learners using only one instructor
options.C: It forces every student to perform a clinical delivery
options.D: It eliminates the need for any physical classroom space

explanation: The main strength of a lecture is that a single teacher can reach a large group of students all at once. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h3)

question: An institution gets an unexpectedly large number of student midwives for a new semester. What is the most practical way to teach core theory right away?

options.A: Suspending all theoretical classes until smaller rooms are built
options.B: Delivering a well-structured lecture to the combined cohort
options.C: Assigning every student a separate online research topic
options.D: Dividing students into pairs for independent hospital shifts

explanation: When class sizes suddenly increase, lecturing is the most practical way to cover baseline material efficiently without needing extra teachers. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h3)

question: Why is the lecture method not ideal for teaching practical midwifery skills like pelvic floor repair?

options.A: It is too expensive for nursing and midwifery schools to fund
options.B: It relies on passive listening rather than hands-on practice
options.C: It forces students to memorize complex chemical formulas
options.D: It requires advanced computers connected to the internet

explanation: Practical skills require physical demonstration and hands-on practice, which cannot be learned by listening to a lecture alone. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h4)

question: What common issue do teachers often notice during long, uninterrupted lectures?

options.A: Learners become overly aggressive and demand extra assignments
options.B: Student attention and concentration drop significantly over time
options.C: Attendance drops to zero within the first five minutes
options.D: Students instantly master all practical delivery room procedures

explanation: Human attention spans are limited, so listening passively for too long naturally leads to tiredness and zoning out. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h4)

question: What is the recommended maximum time for a single continuous block of teaching during a lecture?

options.A: Exactly two hours
options.B: Thirty seconds
options.C: About fifteen minutes
options.D: Four full hours

explanation: Breaking lecture content into short blocks helps students stay focused and avoids overloading their minds. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h5)

question: Why should a midwifery lecture start with an engaging introduction and a review of past topics?

options.A: To connect new clinical ideas to what students already know
options.B: To waste time while late students find seats in the hall
options.C: To prevent the need for any summary at the end of class
options.D: To test whether students bought the required textbooks

explanation: Linking new information to things students have already learned helps them build a better understanding of clinical concepts. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h5)

question: Which of the following is a simple way to break the routine of a quiet lecture?

options.A: Speaking in a flat, unchanging monotone voice
options.B: Dismissing the class twenty minutes early every day
options.C: Forbidding students from writing any notes down
options.D: Pausing for a quick peer discussion or poll

explanation: Short interactive pauses or polls stop passive listening and get students actively thinking about the material. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h6)

question: A lecturer notices students in the back row dozing off during a talk on placental abruption. What is the best immediate response?

options.A: Turn off all the lights in the lecture hall to help them rest
options.B: Introduce a short interactive question or shift vocal tone
options.C: Ignore them and speak even faster to finish the slides
options.D: Stop teaching entirely and send all sleeping students home

explanation: Changing your pace, altering your voice tone, or asking a quick question helps wake up tired students without stopping the whole class. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h6)

question: What is a major problem with putting too much text on presentation slides?

options.A: It improves student retention of every single word
options.B: It automatically repairs damaged projection screens
options.C: It speeds up the overall delivery of the lecture
options.D: It causes cognitive overload for the learners

explanation: When slides are packed with text, students find it hard to read the screen and listen to the instructor at the same time. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h7)

question: Why are short video clips of labor mechanisms a helpful addition to a midwifery lecture?

options.A: They eliminate the need for any clinical hospital postings
options.B: They translate abstract descriptions into clear visual reality
options.C: They prove that textbooks are completely useless for students
options.D: They guarantee that students will never fail an exam

explanation: Videos allow students to see moving biological processes that can be hard to picture from static drawings or text. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of doing a quick comprehension check during a lecture?

options.A: To identify immediate comprehension gaps among students
options.B: To determine final semester grades and graduation status
options.C: To eliminate the need for any future examinations
options.D: To punish students who arrived late to the classroom

explanation: Formative assessments are quick checks used during a class to see if students understand the topic before moving on. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h8)

question: Why is a post-lecture quiz or case study assignment helpful for student midwives?

options.A: It reinforces memory and checks long-term theoretical retention
options.B: It forces students to memorize medical terminology without meaning
options.C: It replaces practical bedside mentorship with paperwork
options.D: It guarantees 100% attendance at all clinical hospital duties

explanation: Follow-up assignments help check whether temporary listening has turned into knowledge that students can remember and use later. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of using the demonstration method in midwifery training?

options.A: To reduce the time spent in hospital wards
options.B: To connect classroom theory with practical clinical skills
options.C: To replace formal written midwifery exams
options.D: To test reading comprehension of textbooks

explanation: Demonstration helps students see how theoretical concepts apply directly to hands-on clinical procedures. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T5#BMP312_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why is visual observation of a procedure critical for midwifery students before trying it themselves?

options.A: It shows correct physical handling, equipment use, and safety steps.
options.B: It eliminates the need for supervised practice sessions.
options.C: It proves clinical documentation expertise.
options.D: It guarantees zero mistakes during real emergency births.

explanation: Watching a skilled performance gives learners a mental model of correct technique and safety measures before their own hands-on attempt. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T5#BMP312_U3_T5_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended step when preparing for a skills demonstration?

options.A: Arranging the room so students have a clear view
options.B: Waiting until students arrive to look for missing supplies
options.C: Defining clear learning objectives for the session
options.D: Gathering and checking all required equipment ahead of time

explanation: Searching for missing items while students are waiting wastes valuable teaching time and disrupts learning flow. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T5#BMP312_U3_T5_h2)

question: A lecturer notices half the class cannot see the pelvis model during a demonstration due to poor seating. What preparation step was missed?

options.A: Proper environment and seating setup for visibility
options.B: Administering a pre-test to check student knowledge
options.C: Checking expiration dates on delivery supplies
options.D: Writing a detailed lesson plan for the theory background

explanation: Arranging the physical space to ensure unobstructed viewing is a vital part of pre-demonstration preparation. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T5#BMP312_U3_T5_h2)

question: How should a midwifery lecturer pace a live clinical skill demonstration for the best learning results?

options.A: Let senior students do the whole demonstration
options.B: Only talk through steps without touching equipment
options.C: Perform it as quickly as possible to save time
options.D: Perform it once fast, then slowly break it down step-by-step with explanations

explanation: Showing the full flow first, followed by a slow, narrated breakdown, helps students grasp both the big picture and the fine details. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T5#BMP312_U3_T5_h3)

question: Why is it important for the lecturer to narrate the 'why' alongside the 'what' during a procedure?

options.A: It prevents students from falling asleep.
options.B: It replaces the need to read textbooks after class.
options.C: It helps students connect clinical actions to underlying anatomical and safety principles.
options.D: It proves the lecturer knows difficult medical terms.

explanation: Explaining the reasoning behind an action builds critical thinking, ensuring students understand clinical safety rather than just copying movements blindly. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T5#BMP312_U3_T5_h3)

question: What is meant by a 'return demonstration' in midwifery education?

options.A: Students return classroom textbooks to the library
options.B: Students perform the skill themselves while the lecturer supervises
options.C: The lecturer repeats the demonstration a second time
options.D: Patients show midwives how they take prescribed medications

explanation: A return demonstration gives the learner a chance to practice and prove they can execute the skill under watchful eyes. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T5#BMP312_U3_T5_h4)

question: Why are small groups and peer coaching helpful during the practice phase of skills lab sessions?

options.A: They ensure weaker students never touch clinical equipment.
options.B: They allow the lecturer to leave the room.
options.C: They reduce the total clinical rotation hours required.
options.D: They increase hands-on practice time and encourage collaborative learning.

explanation: With limited models in busy labs, small groups keep students active and engaged through shared practice and peer feedback. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T5#BMP312_U3_T5_h4)

question: What tool should midwifery educators use to ensure objective grading during practical skill assessments?

options.A: Written multiple-choice question papers at term end
options.B: Random guessing based on general classroom behavior
options.C: Subjective personal memory of student performance
options.D: Standardized evaluation checklists with critical procedure steps

explanation: Checklists ensure every student is graded against the same professional standard, making assessment fair and reliable. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T5#BMP312_U3_T5_h5)

question: A student finishes practicing a perineal suture repair but misses a key aseptic step. How should the lecturer provide feedback?

options.A: Ignore the mistake completely to avoid hurting feelings
options.B: Report the student for professional misconduct
options.C: Praise good suturing speed, then politely point out the missed aseptic step with a correction
options.D: Tell the student the entire procedure was a total failure

explanation: Balanced, constructive feedback acknowledges strengths while offering clear guidance on how to fix specific errors safely. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T5#BMP312_U3_T5_h5)

question: What is a negative consequence of allowing large, overcrowded groups around a single demonstration table?

options.A: All students finish return demonstrations in record time
options.B: The room becomes too cold for comfortable practice
options.C: Manikin models break down from excessive touching
options.D: Students at the back cannot see properly and lose concentration

explanation: Overcrowding blocks visibility and hearing, turning an active demonstration into a passive, ineffective lecture. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T5#BMP312_U3_T5_h6)

question: How does maintaining a supportive, non-punitive tone in the skills lab help midwifery students learn better?

options.A: It eliminates the need for infection control guidelines.
options.B: It ensures no student ever fails a practical exam.
options.C: It lowers anxiety so students feel safe to practice and learn from mistakes.
options.D: It allows students to skip difficult procedures.

explanation: Fear of harsh judgment freezes learners and impedes the trial-and-error process essential for mastering motor skills. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T5#BMP312_U3_T5_h6)

question: What is the main goal of bedside teaching in midwifery?

options.A: To test students without supervision
options.B: To replace traditional classroom lectures entirely
options.C: To connect theoretical knowledge with practical patient care
options.D: To reduce the workload of senior staff nurses

explanation: Bedside teaching brings classroom concepts directly to the ward so students can see and practice real care. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why is bedside teaching different from a normal classroom lecture?

options.A: It prevents students from making any clinical mistakes
options.B: It removes the need for patient consent during tutorials
options.C: It allows students to pass exams without studying theory
options.D: It exposes learners to the authentic environment of maternity units

explanation: Real clinical settings provide practical experience with actual patients that a classroom cannot fully replicate. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h1)

question: Which of these is a key focus during clinical bedside teaching?

options.A: Memorizing textbook definitions without patient interaction
options.B: Managing the hospital budget and drug inventory
options.C: Developing systematic physical assessment and history-taking skills
options.D: Writing formal research papers for hospital administration

explanation: Bedside teaching focuses on hands-on clinical skills like physical exams and talking to patients. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h2)

question: How does bedside teaching help students build good communication skills?

options.A: By forcing them to memorize medical terminology in silence
options.B: By letting them practice speaking empathetically with women in pain or anxiety
options.C: By limiting their conversations strictly to written documentation
options.D: By teaching them how to lecture large groups of people

explanation: Interacting directly with real patients teaches students how to offer emotional comfort and clear explanations. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h2)

question: What is the first thing an instructor should do with a patient before starting a bedside teaching session?

options.A: Ask her to fill out a written examination paper
options.B: Ask for clear permission to involve students in her care
options.C: Begin examining her abdomen without speaking
options.D: Move her to a private lecture hall away from the ward

explanation: Patients must always give consent before they are included in clinical teaching sessions. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h3)

question: Why is it helpful to brief the student before meeting the patient at the bedside?

options.A: It prevents the patient from asking any questions
options.B: It eliminates the need for any supervision by the instructor
options.C: It gives the learner time to review relevant clinical knowledge and focus
options.D: It ensures the student can perform the delivery completely alone

explanation: Knowing the focus beforehand helps students pay attention to the right clinical signs during the session. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h3)

question: How should instructors and students view the patient during a bedside teaching session?

options.A: As an active participant deserving full respect and privacy

options.D: As a public spectator watching a demonstration

question: Which of these actions goes against patient dignity during clinical teaching?

options.A: Discussing the patient's condition across her bed as if she were not present

options.C: Exposing only the specific area needed for a physical check
options.D: Asking for permission before letting a student palpate the abdomen

explanation: Talking about a patient as if she is absent strips away her dignity and ignores her presence. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h4)

question: When is clinical feedback most helpful for a student midwife?

options.A: At the end of the semester during final written exams

options.C: Immediately or very close to the time the action occurred

explanation: Prompt feedback helps students connect the comments directly to what they just did. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h5)

question: A student struggles with an abdominal palpation during a bedside session. What is the best way for the instructor to handle this?

options.A: Stop teaching entirely and take over all patient care duties

options.C: Scold the student loudly so other patients know standards are high
options.D: Wait until the end of the rotation weeks later to mention it

explanation: Gentle, immediate guidance protects patient confidence while helping the student learn safely. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h5)

question: What is a common challenge when doing bedside teaching in busy Nigerian health facilities?

question: What should an instructor do if a sudden ward emergency interrupts a teaching session?

options.A: Punish the students for being present during the emergency

options.C: Cancel all future clinical teaching in the hospital permanently
options.D: Pause the lesson gracefully, attend to the emergency, and resume later if possible

question: What is the typical size range for a small learning group in midwifery education?

question: Why is small group discussion considered superior to traditional lecturing for building teamwork skills?

options.A: It ensures all students receive the exact same grade automatically.
options.B: It requires students to talk, listen, and solve problems together collaboratively.
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for an educator in the classroom.
options.D: It allows students to finish their coursework much faster.

explanation: Interactive peer discussions mirror the communication required in actual healthcare team settings. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T7#BMP312_U3_T7_h1)

question: How does constructivist learning theory support small group discussions?

options.A: It suggests students learn best when memorizing texts in absolute silence.
options.B: It proves that teachers should never interfere once a lesson has started.
options.C: It claims clinical skills can only be learned through watching videos.
options.D: It states learners build understanding best through active engagement and social interaction.

explanation: Constructivism emphasizes that knowledge is actively constructed by the learner through experiences and discussion with others. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T7#BMP312_U3_T7_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a primary benefit of small group discussions for student midwives?

options.A: Encourages respect for different clinical perspectives among peers

options.C: Provides a lower-stakes environment for quieter students to speak

explanation: While group work improves skills and understanding, it cannot single-handedly guarantee examination success without individual study. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T7#BMP312_U3_T7_h2)

question: How should chairs be arranged to best support a small group discussion session?

options.A: In two long lines facing completely away from each other
options.B: In strict rows facing the front chalkboard
options.C: In a circle or around a table to encourage direct eye contact

explanation: A circular seating arrangement breaks down hierarchy and ensures every group member can see and speak to one another easily. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T7#BMP312_U3_T7_h3)

question: An educator wants to prepare a small group session on postpartum care. What is the most important first step?

explanation: Every educational activity starts with a defined objective to guide task creation and keep the discussion focused. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T7#BMP312_U3_T7_h3)

question: How does the primary role of the educator change during a small group discussion?

question: A student group gets stuck on a difficult question about shoulder dystocia. How should the facilitator respond?

question: What is a major challenge of having a dominant speaker in a small group discussion?

options.C: They automatically increase the overall grade point average of the entire cohort.

question: An educator notices that one student is dominating the conversation while another is completely silent. What is an appropriate intervention?

options.C: Directly invite the quiet student to share their thoughts on the clinical case.

question: Why is a plenary debriefing session essential at the end of small group work?

options.A: It prevents students from leaving with incorrect clinical assumptions.

question: How is student performance typically assessed during small group discussions?

question: What is the primary purpose of simulation-based education in midwifery training?

question: Why is simulation especially useful when clinical placement sites are overcrowded?

question: What is a major advantage of using a low-fidelity pelvic model for midwifery students?

question: What must an educator define first when building a new simulation scenario?

options.A: Clear learning objectives
options.B: The budget for buying props

question: An educator is planning a simulation for first-year students who have never managed a delivery. What is the most appropriate step to take?

options.A: Design an advanced crisis scenario involving multiple simultaneous complications

question: Why is a pre-simulation briefing session important for midwifery students?

options.A: It determines which students will fail the upcoming professional exams

options.C: It eliminates the need for any post-simulation feedback

question: What should a facilitator do when students begin to struggle slightly during an active scenario?

question: What is the primary focus of a constructive debriefing session after a simulation?

question: A midwifery school has zero budget for expensive computerized manikins. How can the educator still run effective simulation sessions?

question: What is the main goal of written exams in midwifery training?

question: Which of these is a classic example of an objective test item?

question: Why should educators avoid trick questions or confusing wording in midwifery exams?
